receipt: Genome-wide Gaussian cis-eQTL scan of Geuvadis (462 samples, 20,427 expressed autosomal genes): RapidGLM 1.6.0 qtl (single-precision permutation scores, the default) against tensorQTL 1.0.10, both with 10,000 permutations
host: One AMD Threadripper PRO 5965WX workstation (Zen 3). Timed work uses one thread per physical core on CPUs 6-21, with SMT siblings 30-45 idle; one thread uses CPU 6, eight use 6-13, twelve use 6-17. Drivers and untimed checks use CPUs 0-5.

protocol.runner: validation/receipts/v1.6.0/run_accepted.sh (stage eqtl_gw) under supervise_accepted.py; controllers are tracked beside the receipts
protocol.cpu_policy: Exclusive Slurm allocation; schedutil governor, boost enabled and SMT enabled, unchanged. Each timed command starts after two ten-second quiet samples. More than 5% other CPU activity on selected cores or any sibling invalidates the command. Host load, other-user processes and vLLM CPU use are retained per command. From the resumed bulk stage on 2026-11-03, a user-authorized runtime service cpuset confines vLLM to CPUs 0-5,22-29,46-47; the reservation receipt records its application and restoration. Earlier accepted measurements retain their original guarded host conditions.
protocol.contention: others_cpu: busy time of the timed CPUs not spent by the measured commands, as a share of those CPUs over the wall time; above 0.05 counts as contended and is re-run.

genotypes.source: E-GEUV-1 genotype release (1000 Genomes phase 1 + Omni-imputed, 465 individuals, GRCh37), https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/fire/E-GEUV-/001/E-GEUV-1/Files/E-GEUV-1/genotypes/; same source and naming as chr22 (docs/GEUVADIS.md)
genotypes.filters: scripts/eqtl_prep_genotypes.sh CHR for chromosomes 1-21 (the chr22 filters): the 462 RNA-seq individuals; biallelic SNVs; called in all 462; MAF >= 0.05; GT only; ID CHR_POS_REF_ALT_b37

genome_wide.built: bcftools concat of chr1-22 .vcf.gz, then plink2 --make-bed and --make-pgen (validation/work/large-runs-pikachu/prepare_genotypes.sh)
genome_wide.join_note: A first join (12:21 UTC) listed the chromosomes in lexicographic order; the set was rejoined in numeric order (12:24 UTC) before any timed use.
genome_wide.tensorqtl_reads: pgen (pgenlib present, as in the chr22 receipt run)

genotypes_note: The 1.4.1 inputs, unchanged; their SHA-256 values were checked against that receipt before the run (receipts/v1.6.0/FULL_INPUT_CHECKS.json).

phenotypes.made_by: scripts/eqtl_prep_expression.py --chr all --n-expr-pcs 36 (this change: --chr all writes every expressed autosomal gene, ordered by chromosome and TSS) into data/expression-genomewide
phenotypes.historical_hash_scope_note: The receipt labels the .bed.gz path but its recorded digest is for the uncompressed BED content.

covariates.note: The 42 covariates of the chr22 receipts, unchanged: genotype PCs 1-5 from chr22 (LD-pruned chr22 SNVs), expression PCs 1-36 from all 20,427 expressed genes, and sex. Keeping them lets the chr22 genes of the genome-wide run be checked against the chr22 receipts.

agreement.definition: scripts/compare_eqtl.py: gene-level p = Beta-approximated permutation p (RapidGLM beta_p, tensorQTL pval_beta); Storey q-values (qvalue defaults); eGenes at q < 0.05; same_lead = share of genes with the same lead variant

chr22_check.reference_stage: qtl stage of this run (single precision, 10,000 permutations)
chr22_check.stream: Permutation k of a phenotype is drawn from a counter-based stream keyed by the seed and the phenotype ID (include/rapidglm/qtl.hpp: keyed_stream(seed, 7, 0, name_key(id)); CisQtlOptions documents that results do not depend on threads or on the other phenotypes of the run). The chr22 genes therefore get the same permutations in the genome-wide run, and their rows are expected to be identical, not merely within Monte Carlo error.

egene_identity.rule: Storey q < 0.05 using the same qvalue interface
